facts.text: Along with the spread of English education, new thoughts, ideas and philosophy spread and Indians were introduced to western thoughts and culture.
facts.quote: Along with spread of english education, there was spread of new thoughts, new ideas, new philosophy. Indians were also introduced to western thoughts and culture.

facts.text: Modern educated Indians felt India's backwardness was due to superstitions, casteism, old customs, class system and lack of critical outlook.
facts.quote: The modern educated Indians became aware that the backwardness of India was due to superstitions, casteism, old customs, class system and lack of critical outlook.

facts.text: They wanted a new society based on the principles of Humanity, Equality, and Fraternity.
facts.quote: And to create a new society based on the principles of Humanity, Equality, and Fraternity.

facts.text: The intellectual awakening in the contemporary society is called 'Indian Rennaissance' (Indian Renaissance).
facts.quote: The intellectual awakening in the contemporary society is called 'Indian Rennaissance'.

facts.text: In 1828, Raja Rammohan Roy established the Brahmo Samaj in Bengal.
facts.quote: In 1828, Raja Rammohan Roy established the Brahmo Samaj in Bengal.

facts.text: Principles of Brahmo Samaj: monotheism, caste and class equality, protest against rituals and following the way of prayers; Roy's ideology of Advaita philosophy developed.
facts.quote: Through it his ideology of Advaita philosophy was developed. Monotheism, caste and class equality, protest against rituals and following the way of prayers were the principles of Brahmo Samaj.

facts.text: Raja Rammohan Roy opposed Sati practice, child marriage and Purdah system and promoted widow remarriage and female education.
facts.quote: He opposed Sati practice, child marriage, Purdah system. He promoted widow remarriage and female education.

facts.text: Raja Rammohan Roy founded Hindu College in Kolkata and created awareness through the newspaper 'Samvad Kaumudi'.
facts.quote: He founded Hindu College in Kolkata. He created public awareness through the newspaper 'Samvad Kaumudi'.

facts.text: Dadoba Pandurang Tarkhadkar established the Paramhansa Sabha in Mumbai in 1848.
facts.quote: Dadoba Pandurang Tarkhadkar established Paramhansa Sabha in Mumbai in 1848.

facts.text: After the Paramhansa Sabha was dissolved, some members founded the Prarthana Samaj; Dadoba's brother Dr.Atmaram Pandurang was its first President.
facts.quote: Later Paramhansa Sabha was dissolved and some of its members founded the Prarthana Samaj. Dadoba's brother, Dr.Atmaram Pandurang, was the first President of Prarthana Samaj.

facts.text: Young graduates from Mumbai University raised the prestige of Prarthana Samaj; Justice Ranade and Dr. R. G. Bhandarkar carried forward its work.
facts.quote: The prestige of the institution increased due to the enrollment of young graduates from Mumbai University. Justice Ranade, Dr. R. G. Bhandarkar carried forward the work of Prarthana Samaj.

facts.text: Principles of Prarthana Samaj: opposition to idol worship, monotheism and opposition to rituals; it stressed devotion and prayers.
facts.quote: The opposition to idol worship, monotheism, opposition to rituals were the principles of Prarthana Samaj. They stressed on devotion and prayers.

facts.text: Prarthana Samaj started an orphanage, women's education institutes, night schools for workers and a society for dalits.
facts.quote: For reforming the society, Prarthana Samaj started orphanage, women's education institutes, night schools for workers and society for dalits.

facts.text: Maharshi Vitthal Ramji Shinde, a member of Prarthana Samaj, established the 'Depressed Classes Mission'.
facts.quote: Maharshi Vitthal Ramji Shinde, a member of Prarthana Samaj, established 'Depressed Classes Mission'.

facts.text: Mahatma Jyotirao Phule started the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873; it worked for a society based on equality, protested against untouchability and advocated education of depressed classes and women.
facts.quote: Mahatma Jyotirao Phule started the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873. Satyashodhak Samaj worked on the principle of formation of society on basis of equality. They protested against untouchability. They advocated education among the depressed classes and women.

facts.text: Mahatma Phule reformed society through books like 'Brahmananche Kasab', 'Gulamgiri', 'Shetkaryacha Asud' and 'Sarvajanik Satya Dharma'.
facts.quote: Mahatma Phule reformed the society through the medium of books like 'Brahmananche Kasab', 'Gulamgiri', 'Shetkaryacha Asud' and 'Sarvajanik Satya Dharma'.

facts.text: Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in 1875.
facts.quote: Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in 1875.

facts.text: Swami Dayanand Saraswati wrote the book 'Satyarth Prakash' as a commentary on Vedas.
facts.quote: He wrote the book 'Satyarth Prakash' as a commentary on Vedas.

facts.text: 'Go Back to the Vedas' was the slogan of Arya Samaj.
facts.quote: 'Go Back to the Vedas' was the slogan of Arya Samaj.

facts.text: Branches of Arya Samaj opened all over India and many education institutions were established through it.
facts.quote: The branches of Arya Samaj were opened all over India. Many education institutions were established through the medium of Arya Samaj.

facts.text: Ramkrishna Mission was established by Swami Vivekananda, a close disciple of Ramkrishna Paramhansa, in 1897.
facts.quote: Ramkrishna Mission was established by Swami Vivekananda, a close disciple of Ramkrishna Paramhansa, in 1897.

facts.text: Ramkrishna Mission worked for help to famine stricken people, patients, medical help to the poor, female education and spiritual growth.
facts.quote: The mission worked for providing help to the famine striken people, patients, medical help to the poor, female education and spiritual growth.

facts.text: Swami Vivekananda, an excellent orator, attended the Parliament of Religions at Chicago in 1893 as representative of Hinduism.
facts.quote: Swami Vivekananda was an excellent orator. He attended the Parliament of Religions at Chicago in 1893 as representative of Hinduism.

facts.text: 'Arise, Awake and stop not till the goal is achieved' was Swami Vivekananda's message to the Indian youth.
facts.quote: 'Arise, Awake and stop not till the goal is achieved' was the message given by him to the Indian youth.

facts.text: The Singh Sabha was established at Amritsar to reform Sikh religion and spread education; later the Akali movement continued this tradition.
facts.quote: The Singh Sabha was established at Amritsar to achieve reforms in Sikh religion. This institute worked for spread of education among the Sikh community ... Later the Akali movement continued their tradition of reformation.

facts.text: Women had no right of education; customs like child marriage, dowry system, sati, keshavapan and opposition to widow remarriage prevailed.
facts.quote: They had no right of education. ... Child marriage, dowry system, sati, keshavapan, opposition to widow remarriage such customs prevailed in the society.

facts.text: Governor Lord Bentinck took help of social reformers like Raja Rammohan Roy to pass the Sati Prohibition Act.
facts.quote: The then Governor Lord Bentinck took help of social reformers like Raja Rammohan Roy to pass the Sati Prohibition Act.

facts.text: Gopal Hari Deshmukh, popularly known as 'Lokhitwadi', advocated gender equality through his writings in 'Shatapatre'.
facts.quote: Gopal Hari Deshmukh, popularly known as 'Lokhitwadi' advocated gender equality through his writings in 'Shatapatre'.

facts.text: In 1848, Mahatma Phule started the first school for girls at Bhide Wada in Pune; his wife Savitribai Phule supported him.
facts.quote: In 1848, Mahatma Phule started the first school for girls at Bhide Wada in Pune. His wife Savitribai Phule supported him.

facts.text: Savitribai Phule faced great criticism from society but continued to work in education.
facts.quote: Savitribai Phule had to face great criticism from the Society but she continued to work in education.

facts.text: Mahatma Phule established the 'Bal Hatya Pratibandhak Gruha' in his own house.
facts.quote: Mahatma Phule established the 'Bal Hatya Pratibandhak Gruha' in his own house.

facts.text: Mahatma Phule conducted a strike of barbers against the custom of shaving the heads of widows.
facts.quote: He conducted a strike of barbers against the custom of shaving the heads of the widows.

facts.text: Pandit Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar, Vishnushastri Pandit and Vireshalingam took special efforts to gain permission for widow remarriage.
facts.quote: For gaining permission to widow remarriage, Pandit Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar, Vishnushastri Pandit, and Vireshalingam took up special efforts.

facts.text: In his newspaper Sudharak, Gopal Ganesh Agarkar gave his staunch opinion about child marriage and law of consent.
facts.quote: In his newspaper, Sudharak, Gopal Ganesh Agarkar gave his staunch opinion about child marriage, law of consent.

facts.text: Maharshi Vitthal Ramji Shinde organised a conference against the practice of Devdasi.
facts.quote: Maharshi Vitthal Ramji Shinde organised a conference against the practice of Devdasi.

facts.text: In her book 'Stri Purush Tulana', Tarabai Shinde fiercely put up her views about women's rights.
facts.quote: In her book, 'Stri Purush Tulana', Tarabai Shinde very fiercely put up her views about women's rights.

facts.text: Maharshi Dhondo Karve started the 'Anath Balikashram', an orphanage for girls; through his efforts the first women's university was set up in the 20th century.
facts.quote: Maharshi Dhondo Karve started the 'Anath Balikashram' an orphanage for girls. ... Through his efforts, the first women's university was set up in the 20th century.

facts.text: Pandita Ramabai founded the Sharada Sadan and took care of disabled children and women.
facts.quote: Pandita Ramabai founded the Sharada Sadan and took up the responsibility of taking care of disabled children and women.

facts.text: Ramabai Ranade started the Nursing course for women through the Seva Sadan Institute and demanded the right to vote for women.
facts.quote: Ramabai Ranade, through the medium of Seva Sadan Institute, started the Nursing course for women. She demanded the right to vote for women.

facts.text: Through articles, Dr.Ambedkar spoke about the injustice towards women; Mahatma Gandhi also advocated education of women.
facts.quote: Through articles, Dr.Ambedkar spoke about the injustice towards women. Mahatma Gandhi also advocated education of women.

facts.text: Abdul Latif started social reform among the Muslim community and established 'The Mohammedan Literary Society' in Bengal.
facts.quote: Abdul Latif started the social reform among the muslim community. He established 'The Mohammedan Literary Society' in Bengal.

facts.text: Sir Sayyad Ahmad Khan founded 'The Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College', which later developed into the 'Aligarh Muslim University'; he advocated western science and technology.
facts.quote: Sir Sayyad Ahmad Khan founded 'The Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College'. It later developed into the 'Aligarh Muslim University'. He advocated western science and technology.

facts.text: In 1915, 'Hindu Mahasabha' was established to give a respectable position to the Hindu community.
facts.quote: In 1915, 'Hindu Mahasabha' was established to give a respectable position to the Hindu community.

facts.text: Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya laid the foundation of 'Banaras Hindu University'.
facts.quote: Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya laid the foundation of 'Banaras Hindu University'.

facts.text: Dr. Keshav Baliram Hedgewar, in 1925, established Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh at Nagpur to set up a disciplinary and virtuous organisation of Hindu youth.
facts.quote: Dr. Keshav Baliram Hedgewar, in 1925, established Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh at Nagpur. Its aim was to set up a disciplinary and virtuous organisation of Hindu youth.

facts.text: V.D.Savarkar built the 'Patit Pawan Temple' at Ratnagiri, open to all castes of Hindu religion; common dining programmes were also arranged.
facts.quote: V.D.Savarkar built the 'Patit Pawan Temple' at Ratnagiri, open to all castes of Hindu religion. Common dining programmes were also arranged.

facts.text: Rabindranath Tagore in the field of literature and C.V.Raman in the field of Science received the Nobel prize.
facts.quote: In the field of literature, Rabindranath Tagore and in the field of Science C.V.Raman received the Nobel prize.
